newsitem.title: USA: Pathfinder space probe lands on Mars.
newsitem.headline: Pathfinder space probe lands on Mars.

text.p: The Pathfinder space probe made a historic landing on Mars on Friday, but scientists were faced with a nailbiting four-hour wait to learn the condition of the craft.

There were shouts of joy in the mission control room at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Pasadena as Pathfinder, with its valuable "Mars Buggy" cargo, ended its epic, 309-million mile (497 million km) journey.

"We're down," a delighted Rob Manning, the mission's Flight Systems Manager, shouted out. His announcement, shortly after 10 a.m. PDT (1700 GMT), was greeted with cheering and clapping as team members hugged each other.

Manning based his statement on an unexpected radio signal received from the spacecraft by a tracking station in Spain. The signal indicated the Pathfinder probe was on the surface of Mars in a stable condition.
But Manning cautioned: "There's still a lot to be done. We're not out of the woods yet."
